most_sensitive.assumption: the cost of equity, and with it the weighted average cost of capital used as the discount rate
most_sensitive.reading: The sensitivity grid under valuation.sensitivity.grid was not computed, so no assumption can be ranked by its measured effect on value; what the calculator does show is the input the whole computation stopped on. The cost of equity is missing because beta and the market value of equity are missing, each for the reason printed under cost_of_capital.missing, and with them the weights of debt and equity and the WACC itself. The legs that exist are the risk-free rate of {cost_of_capital.risk_free_rate.value|pct}, the equity risk premium of {cost_of_capital.equity_risk_premium.value|pct} and a pre-tax cost of debt of {cost_of_capital.pre_tax_cost_of_debt.value|pct} on total debt of {ratios.solvency.total_debt.value}, against net debt of only {ratios.solvency.net_debt.value}, so the equity leg would carry nearly all of the weight once it exists. Every scenario's value and the reverse DCF are undefined until this input is supplied, which makes the discount rate the assumption the result depends on before any operating driver.

most_sensitive.assumption: the operating margin path, year one to year ten
most_sensitive.reading: Among the operating drivers, the margin path carries the widest spread between the scenarios relative to the company's own record, so it is the driver whose choice would move the result most once a discount rate exists; without the grid that ordering is a reading of the assumptions, not a computed sensitivity. The record runs from fiscal 2020's {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.5.operating_margin|pct} to the fiscal 2022 peak of {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.3.operating_margin|pct}, then down through fiscal 2023's {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.2.operating_margin|pct} and fiscal 2024's {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.operating_margin|pct} to fiscal 2025's {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_margin|pct}, and the trailing four-quarter margin of {ratios.profitability.operating_margin.value|pct} still carries fiscal 2025's impairments. The base and bull margins rest instead on the quarter's operating income of {ratios.growth.operating_income.this_quarter.value} on revenue of {ratios.growth.revenue.this_quarter.value} and a gross margin of {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.gross_margin.value|pct}, the highest of the filled quarters, which the MD&A describes for the largest segment as "Operating margins increased from 14.9% in the second quarter of 2025 to 21.4% in the second quarter of 2026 primarily due to volume leverage, operational execution and favorable price and product mix from the electronics products and the semiconductor businesses". The bear's terminal margin sits just under fiscal 2020's, the bull's at the fiscal 2022 peak, and the base between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2021; first-year revenue growth has the next widest spread, from the mid single digits to the low twenties against a three-year compound of {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct} and a five-year compound of {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_five_year_compound|pct}, but with a straight-line fade to a common band of terminal rates its weight in a ten-year model is smaller than the margin's.
